correctness.rationale: The ordered tuple orbit is determined by counts of column patterns after translation by its first vertex; extending gives precisely all ordered nonnegative splits of those counts, including repeat vertices. The atomic diagram records clipped distances and the set of next types gives exactly the next EF rank. For remaining rank r, clipping each parent count at 2^(r+1) preserves the feasible splits clipped at 2^r: a saturated count can realize every one-small/one-saturated pair or two saturated children. The base cap 2 suffices for equality and adjacency. Thus all dimensions ≥16 have the same one-vertex rank-three profile and hence root rank-four type by transitivity. A new exact implementation compared nested profiles for dimensions 1–17 and found representatives 1,2,3,4,5,6 with identical profiles at 6–17, bridging the finite range to the lemma. Replay: branches/1d8a83cb-c95f-47f3-a4f3-3ad4945f8a6a/independent_profile_check.py and independent_profile_check_output.txt. Exact objects, not just hashes, were compared. Degree ≥2 and ≥3, two closed neighborhoods, diameter ≤4, and coverage by two radius-two balls are correctly ranked separators; the last fails from d=6 since 2(1+d+binom(d,2))<2^d. Hence the six classes and sharp in-family bound 64 are correct. Frozen source/output inspected only; attestation, prior independent audit, and Lean channels were not performed.
